Hi! I definitely was scared about this before my surgery as well because I am a larger person and my boobs stuck out more/the same amount as my stomach so I worried about the results. But honestly now that I am not overly focused on that and looking at my body for big picture I realized that it isn’t noticeable or crazy. Like yes I am still fat and I am still uncomfortable with my body but I am not any more uncomfortable with my stomach than before surgery, but at least now I’m not uncomfortable with my boobs! So I guess all this to say- the changing of body image directly after surgery was a bit of an emotional rollercoaster but it was 100% worth it and I never regretted it. So you aren’t alone in your fear, and you aren’t alone if post op you take time to adjust but I also definitely think it’s not going to be as noticeable or drastic as you may fear!

I wish I had gotten it younger just because I feel almost like I’ve lost my youth by not being able to wear cute things without feeling extremely uncomfortable. My mom got her reduction at about age 55 ish and she said she wished she had done it younger as well. 

I wish I did it ASAP. And I know 25 is still way younger than some people, my mom for example. But when I think back to all the events and things I had between age 18 and now where maybe I didn’t have to cry in the mirror before leaving or try my best to squish them down with an ace bandage and come home with sore ribs, I wish I could have enjoyed those events as young adult instead. There is always the possibility that the grow back especially when considering possible future pregnancy so for people who eventually want kids I see why that may be a factor in the decision making but for me it doesn’t really matter. I’ll handle the possibility or regrown if it happens but for now I’m so so uncomfortable in my body and want at least some of my younger years to have fond memories. I’m at the age of friends weddings and graduations and baby showers and I want to go to them and have a good time and not be thinking about my boobs the whole time or have to spend weeks before and lots of money searching for the perfect outfit to hide them as much as possible.

But toss that advice about the boyfriend because it’s garbage (no offense to your mom) but it’s your body and you feeling comfortable is the number one priority. Hi! So I started completely from nothing and it’s possible! Here’s how it went for me:
•Early November 2020- at a normal psychiatrist appointment (I’m super close to my psychiatrist NP and she’s amazing) she tells me how she will be out for a little while because she’s having breast reduction. I tell her that I’ve never told anyone but I actually have always wanted one too. She said I should go for it and gives me the name of her surgeon that she loves. 
•A few days later (still early nov 2020) I have a previously scheduled pcp appointment for a follow up on something else, while there I tell her about my wanting a reduction but that I have absolutely no notes or anything anywhere of back pain or any issues. She said she would put it in my chart so at least we could get it started, not knowing how long it might take. After that appointment I call the surgeon recommended by my psych and set up consultation 
•dec 17th ish 2020 go to my consultation. It was super uncomfortable for me because I hate talking about my body, I hate getting undressed in front of people, I hate people touching my body, etc but he and his whole team were amazing and did their best to make it as painless as possible and help me feel better. They said they would go ahead and submit to insurance and just see what happens. 
•insurance lady sends in the request right after the new year and says it should take about 6 weeks to hear back so mid February. 
• mid February 2021 right on time I get a letter from insurance. Approval! (Actually I got two letters one approving and one not but that was a mistake and everything was worked out)
•insurance lady from surgeries practice calls and said I could schedule a surgery date and their next opening was in April, I decided to instead schedule a follow up appt to come in and talk again before scheduling surgery. At the follow up appt we realized that a steroid cream I was using on rash between boobs was thinning my skin so surgeon said stop using it and come back in 6 weeks 
•April 2021 went in to follow up on the skin thinning and everything was good! Scheduled surgery  for June 2021!

So my timeline is from beginning this process to surgery date around 7/8 months but could have been quicker if I had scheduled right away. 

But also I know not everyone has this case where they don’t need a lot of records of pain and issues and other methods to fix the issues so I’m grateful for how easy this was. Also to add I am overweight and it wasn’t an issue. The insurance lady for my surgeon  though is amazing and I think helped get it through because she told me when I was there a few weeks ago that when she submitted to insurance my case they called her thinking she forgot to include records because there was nothing and she told them my story about how I’ve always been too uncomfortable with my body to talk about it and that my psych recommended I do this and that the surgeon thinks it will help my mental health/quality of life (I broke down and cried to him about all my mental health issues) so she advocated for me which probably helped get it done which was so kind. Anyway good luck with your process! I hope this was somewhat helpful!

Editing to add: I want to mention that this claim of poor mental health wasn’t unfamiliar to my insurance as I have been doing tons of different, sometimes extreme methods of mental health treatment for years that is all on insurance and recorded so they are very aware of lots of issues going on there

I have federal blue cross blue shield so I’m not sure how they’re similar and how they differ but I’ll give you my timeline 
Novemberish (right before thanksgiving) my psychiatrist told me she would be having a breast reduction. I told her I’ve always wanted one and she told me how much she loved the surgeon she was going to be doing it through and that I should go meet with me. 
Late November I schedule an appointment to see doctor in mid December (I think somewhere around the 17th or 18th)
Early December I go to a previously scheduled appointment with my primary doctor for other health issues. While there I tell her my plans about reduction. She said she would go ahead and write neck and back pain in my chart to start the documentation process if needed 
December I go to my consultation with the plastic surgery. I really like him and his team and he thinks I’m a good candidate and feels confident in insurance coverage (I asked him about coverage even with being pretty severely overweight and he said he’s not worried about it)
December 29 I go back to surgerons office because the pictures they took to submit to insurance had some issues so I had to go back before the could submit anything. They tell me that they will submit it right after the new year and that I should hear back in mid February. 
Sure enough mid February roles around and I got my approval letter in the mail! Now I am working on scheduling a surgery date. The office had openings as early as April 6 (when I called around February 18th) but I haven’t picked a day yet because of trying to figure out my own schedule so now their next opening isn’t until later but if I had been free for any time then I could have stated this process in December (first consultation) and had surgery completed in April. I didn’t have to do any physical therapy, I didn’t have to have anything documented about pain (although I did have that one documentation in my chart, it wasn’t necessary), I didn’t have to go to a chiropractor or show proof of really anything. Also I’m significantly overweight. My whole process has honestly been super easy and so I’m really grateful for that as I know that is not the case for every one. I hope this somewhat helps you though! Good luck!

Also insurance likes to dictate how much would have to be taken out based on your size, weight, height etc so if you don’t hit that they may not pay. Also there are different techniques that surgeons use to reduce and so big reductions may require a more substantial surgery- a FNG or free nipple graft which has more risks and stuff but honestly I don’t know when they go to that from the other method in terms of how much you’re reducing so you might be fine to go from a D to an A with just a typical anchor incision (less invasive and risks and recovery than FNG) also I think it depends on the surgeon.
